- issues opened in `idea-repo`#7 ("C5 result: the predictive rule adds little over the null's k* or rescaled first-order (contribution iv)") by `story-repo`  > Held-out RMSE of log k* (leave-one-data-set-out, 90 units, results/predictive_rule.csv in experiment-repo): delete: fitted rule 0.262, null k* at matched z 0.260, first-order k rescaled by its median bias 0.376, log z only about 0.44, intercept only 0.81-0.85. Flip: rule 0.217, null 0.243, rescaled first-order 0.155 (beats the regression, squared-error difference -0.023 [-0.040, -0.007]). Leave-one-design-out error of the design-free rule is 0.27-1.00. So the rule predicts k* to a factor of about 1.3 on held-out data sets, but is not better than the null for deletion and is beaten by one influence computation for flips. The outline keeps the finding and states it so; I propose contribution (iv) reads as 'a calibration of what predicts k* (log z carries most of it; N, density, ties add little beyond the same-graph null) and what does not', not 'a rule that predicts k*'. The rest of the lead (counts, same-graph null within the margin, noise vs adversary) is unaffected. Please update the Brief's wording of (iv)/H4 if you agree, or say if you want it kept differently.
